sections.heading: Learning to drive: first part — B
sections.markdown:
Audience and scope: learning to drive: first part within the selected first-time passenger-car knowledge preparation path. This is an authoring scope from the pinned run configuration.
Coverage plan: Starting moving and stopping; Steering and backing; Intersections and turns; Red-light turns and intersection gaps; Roundabouts and lane travel. These are authored organizational labels, with no official examination weighting or eligibility assertion.
Starting, normal stopping, emergency-vehicle response, steering, backing, turns, roundabouts and lane-position exceptions are represented. Arm-signal figures have no extracted posture description and remain a visual gap. The lane-change heading continues on the next mapped section. The left-turn-at-green wording and roundabout exit pattern are retained as source-qualified statements, not expanded into universal permissions.

sections.heading: Learning to drive: first part — C
sections.markdown:
FACT_ID: sec05-F01 | anchor: A33
Check the vehicle owner's manual for its starting instructions. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec05-F02 | anchor: A33
To start the described automatic vehicle, hold the brake with your right foot, verify the selector is in park, and turn the ignition key or press Start. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec05-F03 | anchor: A33
Select drive, check ahead, beside and behind for traffic, signal, and move from brake to accelerator only when the path is safe. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec05-F04 | anchor: A33
Accelerate gently with the ball of your foot on the pedal and your heel resting on the floor. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec05-F05 | anchor: A33
For a normal stop, check rear traffic in the mirrors, move from accelerator to brake and maintain steady brake pressure until stopped. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec05-F06 | anchor: A33
Stopping distance depends on reaction time, travel speed, brake condition and pavement condition. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec05-F07 | anchor: A33
Keep a following interval of three to four seconds behind the vehicle ahead. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec05-F08 | anchor: A33
Before entering an intersection at a stop sign or red light, stop behind the stop line or crosswalk. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec05-F09 | anchor: A33
Even when a red-light turn is permitted, first stop completely behind the stop line or crosswalk and yield to crossing traffic and pedestrians. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec05-F10 | anchor: A33
Stop at a flashing red signal and yield to traffic that is not required to stop. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec05-F11 | anchor: A33
In a business or residential district, stop at the sidewalk when leaving an alley, driveway or private road, or before the roadway if there is no sidewalk, and yield to sidewalk pedestrians. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec05-F12 | anchor: A34
Stop before an intersection when there is not enough space beyond it for your vehicle, even if the signal permits movement. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec05-F13 | anchor: A34
For an approaching public-safety vehicle using flashing lights and an audible warning, move as far right as possible and remain stopped until it passes, except when it approaches from the opposite side of a divided highway. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec05-F14 | anchor: A34
Turn the steering wheel toward the desired direction of travel whether moving forward or backward. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec05-F15 | anchor: A34
Place both hands on opposite outer sides of the wheel at four and eight o'clock, using a firm but gentle grip for control and air-bag clearance. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec05-F16 | anchor: A34
Look behind the vehicle before getting in because the driver's seat may hide children or small objects. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec05-F17 | anchor: A34
Keep a foot on the brake when shifting the vehicle into reverse. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec05-F18 | anchor: A34
For backing, place the left hand at twelve o'clock on the wheel and the right arm along the passenger seat back while looking through the rear window. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec05-F19 | anchor: A35
Mirrors used during backing do not show the area directly behind the vehicle. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec05-F20 | anchor: A35
Use a rear-view camera when available, but do not depend on it alone because it may omit part of the area. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec05-F21 | anchor: A35
Back slowly with gentle acceleration, turning the wheel slightly toward the desired rearward path because steering is harder in reverse. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec05-F22 | anchor: A35
When backing through a turn, briefly check ahead and to the sides while continuing to look rearward until fully stopped. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec05-F23 | anchor: A35
At every intersection, slow down and check traffic controls, pedestrians, pavement conditions and places where visibility is limited. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec05-F24 | anchor: A35
Check oncoming and crossing traffic, including motorcycles and bicycles, by looking left, right and left again. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec05-F25 | anchor: A35
Before turning, signal, check every corner for traffic and controls, and position the vehicle in the lane nearest the intended direction. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec05-F26 | anchor: A35
Look as far along the intended turning path as possible. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec05-F27 | anchor: A35
After a turn, accelerate smoothly to a suitable speed, cancel the signal and check traffic behind. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec05-F28 | anchor: A35
Signal at least one hundred feet before a turn using the vehicle signal or the appropriate arm signal. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec05-F29 | anchor: A36
Do not swing left before making a right turn. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec05-F30 | anchor: A36
Turn right from the far-right part of your lane into the far-right part of the destination street. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec05-F31 | anchor: A36
Yield to oncoming traffic before making a left turn. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec05-F32 | anchor: A36
Turn left from the far-left part of your lane into the destination lane farthest left but just right of its center divider, including on four-lane highways. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0036]

sections.heading: Learning to drive: first part — C2
sections.markdown:
FACT_ID: sec05-R01 | anchor: A37
The handbook directs a left-turning driver at green to wait for a turning opportunity; if heavy traffic prevents one, it describes placing the vehicle's front slightly beyond the stop bar, yielding to pedestrians and opposing traffic, and turning when safe. [A37]
Source: [A37 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec05-R02 | anchor: A37
Enter the intended turning lane before the turn and remain in that lane until the turn is finished. [A37]
Source: [A37 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec05-R03 | anchor: A37
A right turn at red is allowed unless a sign forbids it, after a complete stop and after all crossing vehicles and pedestrians clear the intersection. [A37]
Source: [A37 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec05-R04 | anchor: A37
A left turn at red is allowed only from the far-left lane of a one-way street into another one-way street, unless a posted sign prohibits that turn. [A37]
Source: [A37 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec05-R05 | anchor: A38
When a light changes to green, wait briefly before entering and do not assume that other road users will obey their signals or yield. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec05-R06 | anchor: A38
Even at green, wait before the intersection until traffic beyond it moves enough to let you clear it without blocking crossing traffic. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec05-R07 | anchor: A38
Before turning onto a road, verify a clear path and a gap large enough to cross, enter the proper lane and accelerate to traffic speed. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec05-R08 | anchor: A38
Do not turn or pull out in front of an approaching signaling vehicle without enough clear distance, because its driver may turn later or have left the signal on. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec05-R09 | anchor: A38
After stopping where cross traffic is hidden, edge forward to obtain a view before entering the intersection. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec05-R10 | anchor: A38
In a roundabout or traffic circle, vehicles move counterclockwise around a raised central island. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec05-R11 | anchor: A38
Check direction signs before entering a roundabout because lane changes are not allowed inside it. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec05-R12 | anchor: A38
Reduce speed before entering a roundabout or traffic circle. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec05-R13 | anchor: A38
Yield to vehicles already circulating before entering a roundabout or traffic circle. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec05-R14 | anchor: A39
Look left for circulating traffic and enter only when the lane is clear. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec05-R15 | anchor: A39
After entering a roundabout, keep moving without stopping or changing lanes. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec05-R16 | anchor: A39
Signal as you reach the appropriate roundabout exit and leave the circle. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec05-R17 | anchor: A39
The handbook's listed roundabout pattern uses the first exit for a right turn. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec05-R18 | anchor: A39
The handbook's listed roundabout pattern uses the second exit to continue straight. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec05-R19 | anchor: A39
The handbook's listed roundabout pattern uses the third exit for a left turn. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec05-R20 | anchor: A39
The handbook's listed roundabout pattern uses the fourth exit to reverse direction with a U-turn. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec05-R21 | anchor: A39
Drive on the roadway's right half unless one of the stated exceptions applies. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec05-R22 | anchor: A39
Passing a vehicle traveling in the same direction is a stated exception to the right-half roadway rule. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec05-R23 | anchor: A39
A road divided into at least three marked lanes is a stated exception to the right-half roadway rule. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec05-R24 | anchor: A39
A road designed and posted for one-way traffic is a stated exception to the right-half roadway rule. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec05-R25 | anchor: A39
Police directions or a traffic-control device may direct travel outside the normal right half of the roadway. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec05-R26 | anchor: A39
An obstruction may require driving left of center, but the driver must yield to oncoming traffic. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec05-R27 | anchor: A39
On a road with at least four lanes, the handbook directs travel in the right lane and use of the lane immediately right of center for passing and left turns. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0039]

Confusables: a permitted red-light turn still requires a complete stop and yielding; a green signal does not provide room beyond a blocked intersection. Mirrors and cameras supplement looking while backing. Mnemonic: search, position, signal, clear. Glossary: a roundabout is a circular intersection; following interval is the time gap behind the leading vehicle. These cues organize the cited statements only.
